newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Charity ditches fake notes in money-mad Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Charity ditches fake notes in money-mad Hong Kong.

text.p: A Hong Kong charity has disappointed money-mad collectors by scrapping plans to make them all paper-millionaires to salute rule by China.
Proposed look-alike banknotes too closely resembled the real thing, authorities advised.
Pok Oi Hospital planned to sell for HK$1,698 (US$189) a set of nine red HK$1 million notes as souvenirs.

Currency denominations here go only as high as HK$1,000, but Hong Kong's Monetary Authority (HKMA) said foreigners may be deceived by the souvenirs, charity spokewoman Catalles Sin told Reuters on Wednesday.
Hong Kong's HK$100 notes are also red - a lucky colour for Chinese.

Prince Charles will hand Hong Kong's sovereignty to President Jiang Zemen on July 1, ending 156 years of colonial rule. The transition has been an enormous media event and many organisations have been trying to cash in on it.
Another set of million-dollar souvenir notes, issued by Money World Asia, is under investigation by the monetary authority as a close imitation, HKMA spokesman Albert Chan said.
The Bank of England printed the second set using its own Debden Security Printing technology and genuine currency paper, an official at Money World Asia has said.
The notes therefore look and feel like the real thing, except that they are not legal tender.
They feature a portrait of late Chinese patriarch Deng Xiaoping, the chief architect of China's econoimic reforms, who died early this year.

Deng, who had wanted to see the Hong Kong handover which will end an era of national shame for China, is seen smiling at the skyscraper backdrop of the territory's famed Victoria Harbour, named after Britain's 19th century empress.
The notes carry the mottos, "Return to the motherland, joy to the world" and "One country, two systems, Hong Kong people rule Hong Kong."
